question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund is an OPEN-ENDED Category III AIF. Per the workbook's Investor Charter and valuation guidance, what NAV disclosure frequency must the fund administrator follow?

answer.text: Annual NAV audited by the statutory auditor

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's Investor Charter and valuation sections state that for an open-ended Category III AIF, NAV must be disclosed to investors on a monthly basis. Close-ended Category III AIFs disclose NAV quarterly. A comparison table elsewhere in the workbook notes NAV declaration may be daily, monthly, or quarterly as specified in the PPM, but the Investor Charter sets the minimum disclosure cadence for open-ended Cat III funds at monthly. The Trap: Quarterly is the cadence for close-ended Cat III AIFs (and for Cat I/II). Daily is permitted if specified in the PPM but is not the mandated minimum disclosure for open-ended Cat III. Annual reflects audit cadence rather than NAV disclosure. Note: Funds may compute and publish NAV more frequently than monthly if the PPM commits to it. The monthly figure is the regulatory floor for open-ended Category III disclosure.
